extracted.intended_audience: marketing and PR professionals and small business owners producing video press releases (VNRs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, producing, hosting, and distributing Video News Releases (VNRs) — video-format press releases used to earn media coverage. Covers when to use VNRs, required elements, production tips, hosting choices, distribution methods, and success metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use cases for VNRs
rubrics_metrics.description: VNRs are video versions of a press release used for important news, announcements, or updates that benefit from motion/visuals (e.g., launching a new product with a demo, showing a new location via video tour, crisis response via spokesperson interview, event recap, software demonstrations, company rebranding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a VNR when visuals or personality add clarity or emotional impact—e.g., a product demo, tour, or interview adds value over text. Avoid VNRs when the story is purely factual and better served by text-only distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential structural elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A VNR should contain an intro, the news content, proof (supporting images/footage), and an outro (including brand logo as final shot).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intro may be host spoken or onscreen text; news content is spoken by host or voice-over; proof includes product demos, tours, interviews; outro should cap the story and finish with brand logo for recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action (CTA) use
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls to action are often present in VNRs advertising products or services but are more subtle than in ads (e.g., factual phrasing like 'the new cafe opens Wednesday…' rather than 'You can visit…').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CTAs sparingly and in news-appropriate phrasing so the video reads like news, not an advertisement. Not all VNRs require CTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview-style videos depict a spokesperson answering questions; best for major announcements that affect many people (C-suite hires, mergers, crisis communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews put a face to the company and communicate important information directly. Keep conversational shots by switching between interviewer and subject; film multiple takes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Product tours / demos
rubrics_metrics.description: Product tours/demos show a problem customers face and demonstrate how the product/service provides a solution; especially useful for complex products (e.g., software).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear problem-solution narrative, close-ups of features, and real-world usage to build credibility and approachability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Testimonials
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimonials feature customers speaking about their experience and provide an objective perspective on what potential customers might expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use genuine, specific customer stories; avoid overly promotional language that undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Sneak peeks / teasers
rubrics_metrics.description: Behind-the-scenes glimpses designed to create buzz about upcoming products or events; typically positive in tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for pre-launch excitement; keep content suggestive rather than fully revealing to build anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Company profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos that present company mission, history, and overview of products/services, often including ways for audiences to learn more (website/social links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best for brand-introduction stories; balance background info with newsworthiness to attract journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of VNR — Interactive videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos prompting viewer interaction (clicks, choices) to learn more; useful for product launches, events, and tracking engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive VNRs provide measurable interactions useful for marketing insights; consider platform compatibility and journalists' needs (some outlets may prefer linear video).

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and pre-production
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a script (pre-production) to guide the video’s direction; for interviews/testimonials a script may include intro, conclusion, and question list; product tours and profiles need shot lists, voice-over scripts, and visual directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripts ensure clarity and consistent messaging. Tailor script detail to VNR type and provide shot lists so production and editing remain focused on the news angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera choice and visual quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a DSLR camera if possible for top-notch visual quality; camera choice affects professional feel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher-quality visuals increase chances of media pickup. For low budgets, modern smartphones can work if other production practices are strong (lighting, tripod, framing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio quality and microphone selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Use high-quality microphones: condenser microphones for general sound/voice-overs and lapel microphones for on-camera speakers to minimize background noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear audio is critical—bad sound reduces pickup. Test audio before recording; if necessary, use wired/Bluetooth earphones only when they yield better sound and remain out of frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lighting
rubrics_metrics.description: Good lighting sets visual quality; natural light is cost-effective but inconsistent—consider artificial lighting for reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subjects are well-lit and avoid harsh shadows. For mobile filming, add lamps or open windows if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera stabilization (tripod)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a tripod or stable base to eliminate shakiness and make the video look professional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no tripod, improvise with books or other supports; stability increases the likelihood of being used by reputable media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background music licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Background music may be used for transitions or mood, but must be properly licensed (copyrighted, royalty-free, or public domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always secure licensing; avoid unlicensed tracks that can cause legal/usage issues for media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleprompter use and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Teleprompters help speakers maintain eye contact and deliver lines; alternatives include using presentation software (PowerPoint/Slides) placed at eye level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teleprompters improve polished delivery for speeches/announcements; improvised teleprompter setups can work for budget shoots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing software and post-production
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing software ranges from basic to advanced (Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, Camtasia, Screencastify, ScreenFlow); choose based on needed sophistication and skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan editing complexity in pre-production; take multiple takes to give editors options. Simpler tools suffice for basic cuts; advanced tools enable professional polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing production & distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider hiring professional video production or distribution services based on budget and desired reach (examples provided with price ranges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsource when you need professional quality or broad distribution and when in-house capabilities/budget are insufficient. Compare cost vs expected PR value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile device filming best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: When filming with smartphones: always use a tripod, film in landscape mode, ensure adequate lighting, test audio options, and use teleprompter alternatives if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smartphone video can be high quality if stable, well-lit, and with good audio. Landscape orientation is critical for screen compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting platform selection (YouTube vs Vimeo)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube offers massive reach and free hosting; Vimeo provides a cleaner, more professional presentation with fewer viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host on the platform that matches your audience—YouTube for discoverability and SEO, Vimeo for a professional embed experience; rename video file with a keyword for optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual distribution vs distribution services
rubrics_metrics.description: Manual emailing allows personalized, targeted pitches to journalists; distribution services enable mass targeting to newswires and journalists for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both methods when possible—personalized pitches for key targets and distribution services for scale. Manual allows relationship-based pitching; services offer reach and convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach vs embed for broadcast distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If distributing to broadcast media, attach the video file to the release rather than embedding it so newsrooms can easily play it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed is fine for online publication; attach when you want the file readily usable by TV/radio newsrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for added distribution costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution services may charge extra for video attachments or embedding, sometimes only offering video features on higher-priced plans (fees up to $300 per asset cited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm pricing for video embedding/attachments before purchasing a distribution plan to avoid surprises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video performance tracking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose services that provide in-depth reporting on video consumption and engagement (downloads, plays, views, view times) and track metrics like journalists’ pickup, leads, sales, view count, engagements, viewing time, and traffic sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary success metric is how many journalists cover your story; supplement with marketing metrics (leads, engagement). Ensure the chosen distributor/platform supplies the specific metrics you need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the newsworthy angle clear
rubrics_metrics.description: VNRs should stick to a newsworthy (not advertorial) angle with an informative, objective tone that promotes a story rather than directly selling a product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft scripts around who, what, why, when, where, and how. Avoid persuasive ad language; present facts and relevance to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a story that matters to the target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the announcement impacts the audience—present a problem, support with facts, and explain the relevance of the announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the VNR so journalists and their readers/viewers see clear audience value. Use anecdotes, data, or testimonials to demonstrate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the video feel ad-free
rubrics_metrics.description: Create the VNR like a news story rather than an advertisement to increase chances of media pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blatant product promotion; lean on objective language, third-party sources, experts, or customer voices to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia assets for journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a variety of multimedia (visual and interactive) assets that journalists can use so they have everything needed to publish the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include B-roll, images, transcripts, and contact info in a press kit to make it easy for newsrooms to run the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film multiple takes of each scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Shoot several takes so editors can choose the best shots and the final video looks professional and coherent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple takes improve final quality and reduce the risk of unusable footage; plan time for retakes in production schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed VNR in published press release
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing a press release on a newswire or website, embed the VNR so viewers don't have to click away to view it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding improves user experience and increases the chance the video is viewed in context; ensure the embed is compatible with publisher platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended VNR length
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep VNRs between one and three minutes long, depending on type, while ensuring all necessary information journalists need is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise—don’t crowd the video with extraneous information, but include sufficient detail to make the story interesting to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core qualities of a good press release (video or text)
rubrics_metrics.description: A good press release is informative, relevant, straightforward, and interesting to the target audience; it answers who, what, when, where, why, and how, is concise, honest, avoids industry jargon, and includes multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain language, prioritize journalist needs, and include contact info and assets to facilitate coverage. Treat the VNR as part of a larger press kit when appropriate.
